commit message:
Implement vtkMRMLIGTLConnectorNode::Persistent

This option represents whether or not a connection should
be persistent across scene saves.

if `persistent == ::PERSISTENT_ON` then the node connects
based on the `::state` setting.

if `persistent == ::PERSISTENT_OFF` then the node does not
reconnect when the scene is loaded.

commit message:
ENH: Prevent continuous changing of connector node state while waiting for connection

igtlcon->WaitForConnection() does not delete the socket, just closes it, so (igtlcon->Socket.IsNotNull()) is always true.
This causes a STATE_WAIT_CONNECTED and STATE_WAIT_CONNECTION state change at each reconnect attempt, which results unnecessary Modified event invocations (that causes for example lots of failed command sending attempts in PlusRemote).

Instead, (igtlcon->Socket->GetConnected()) should be called to see if a client/server is connected successfully.

Tested on Windows in both client and server modes.

ENH: Enhancements for better OpenIGTLink string command support

* Use simple vtkMRMLTextNode instead of vtkMRMLAnnotationTextNode
* Implemented query timeout (timeout was already in the query node but it was not used): state of the query changes to TIMEOUT if allowed time is expired
* Implemented STRING query for commands: if a STRING query node contains CommandDeviceName and CommandString attributes then a STRING message is sent out with this content as a query
* Allow the query node to have any name: IGTLDeviceName attribute is used instead of the node Name for matching with incoming nodes (NoNameQuery is not needed anymore, IGTLDeviceName can be set to empty instead)
* Use node references in vtkMRMLIGTLQueryNode instead of storing node IDs

commit message:
BUG: Fix hang when sending a blocking command in response to a connection

Sending a blocking command will attempt to call PeriodicProcess again to force the command to be sent. This can cause a deadlock if it is sent in response to an event due to the lock on EventQueueMutex.
Fixed by converting EventQueueMutex to a recursive_mutex since multiple same-thread access to EventQueue seems safe.

so X1 and X6 are no longer the correct names.

commit message:
speeding up SprintDataset

This approach helps a lot. This makes it as fast as it was in 0ed3d93.
Note that 0ed3d93 (before the shuffle frame support) was broken,
because the locks were not used correctly in assign_dev_data().

Most Python functions will release the GIL.
However, most notably, some Numpy functions will not, such as concatenate.

Numpy, concatenate:
  https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/numpy/core/src/multiarray/multiarraymodule.c
  no GIL release!

CPython, thread.lock:
  https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/master/Modules/_threadmodule.c
  GIL release.

CPython, Connection.recv, conn_recv_string:
  https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/2.7/Modules/_multiprocessing/socket_connection.c
  GIL release.

CPython, Connection.poll, connection_poll:
  https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/2.7/Modules/_multiprocessing/connection.h
  GIL release.

Some numbers for an 8 layer relu net trained with adadelta:

before shuffle frames:
  fast
  1: 15.83%, 6:50
  1: 18.32%, 7:46
  2: 5.90%, 1:44 -> 17.64sec/% (GTX TITAN)

after, sprint cache 5/10:
  10.17%, 25:18

after, …, alloc no lock:
  6.40%, 4:17
  17.60%, 14:51

after, less locks (5046f):
  2: 8.39%, 6:09 -> 43.98sec/% (GTX TITAN)
  3: 14.05%, 10:31 -> 44.91sec/% (GTX TITAN)
  4: 3.1%, 1:51 -> 35.81sec/% (GTX TITAN)

after data queue:
  5: 6.35%, 1:56 -> 18.27sec/% (GTX TITAN)
  5: 15.52%, 4:32 -> 17.53sec/% (GTX TITAN)

commit message:
LmDataset, simplify use of word boundaries in character-based modeling

Add `word_end_symbol` option.
When `word_based` is set to False and word_end_symbol is specified,
automatically replaces the spaces by word_end_symbol.
word_end_symbol must be in the character-level vocabulary.

The word_end_symbol is also inserted after the last word in a sentence
before the `seq_end_symbol`.

Simplify for example:
https://github.com/rwth-i6/returnn-experiments/issues/19

commit message:
CombinedDataset, multiple fixes

Multiple issues:

* `num_seqs = sum([self.datasets[k].num_seqs for ...])`
is wrong in general. num_seqs can change for each epoch.
Cleaned up all related code.

* rnd.seed was missing in init_seq_order, thus the dataset
behaved non-deterministic.

* `for dataset_seq_idx in range(dataset.num_seqs)`
is wrong. That is not how you would loop over the seq indices.
But anyway, this code becomes obsolete.

* There might be more issues with this dataset...

commit message:
get GCC version, some further heuristic

It's really only a heuristic.
This is only used if there is no matching major version,
where we just gave up before.
So it might potentially only improve things.

In my particular case, I had GCC 7, 8, 9 installed,
and TF was compiled with GCC 5, and used CUDA 10.0.
This is the official TF 1.14 from pip.
RETURNN picked GCC 9, which did not work together with the nvcc from CUDA 10.0,
which required GCC <=7.
So this heuristic fixes this particular case.
At least it compiles now, and all tests (from test_TFNative) seem to pass.

commit message:
remove/cleanup Data.undefined and CannotHandleUndefinedSourcesException

Also make sure that get_layer never returns None.

This was a wrong direction.
It just made transform_config_dict and get_out_data_from_opts
more complicated for every single layer.

The new logic is simply:
During template construction, if some input is unknown,
just return some dummy input layer / input data.

Note that we already had this logic before,
but the template construction could end up with incorrect data.
Now the template construction,
more specifically the rec layer template construction
has extra logic whether some constructed layer
was based on incomplete/dummy input,
and it will recreate it later again.
This seems to be fine now.
(At least all tests are passing...)

I think this is in general a better direction in any case:
Keep get_out_data_from_opts and transform_config_dict simple
and straight-forward.
Use dummy inputs if it is unknown, and cleverly resolve it later.

There are many ways how the template construction could be resolved.
The current logic works, but is maybe still not optimal.
Once we get to further problems there, this can be extended.

author: Frithjof <fmpetrick@gmail.com>
commit message:
SelfAttention: Use separate prev key / value when in loop (#348)

This reduces memory footprint when in loop.

When inside a recurrent loop, store a single prev_k and prev_v instead of a concatenation
prev_kv. This saves a split-operation of the prev_kv-tensor with length (t-1) at time step t
into separate prev_k and prev_v, thus having a quadratic memory footprint in t.

commit message:
Generic LayerBase in_dim and out_dim options (#765)

#597

in_dim is checked for many common cases
for verification in LayerBase
(just that the dim exists in the input,
if there is a single input).

in_dim is also used in _ConcatInputLayer
to define the concatenated feature dim.

out_dim is further used for verification
in LayerBase (just that the dim exists in the output).

out_dim is used for layers which rely on
_base_get_out_data_from_opts,
e.g. LinearLayer
to define the output feature dim.

out_dim is used by CopyLayer
to define a potential new concatenated output feature dim.

commit message:
CombineLayer, ignore sparse flag

Note that before this change, sth like a + b was possible
for sparse tensors a and b, and it was adding their values,
i.e. not interpreting them as dense tensors.

With this change, now a + b is possible when a is sparse
and b is not.

E.g. when a is the index in a dim (via argmax or so)
and b is just an offset,
b would usually not be declared as sparse.

commit message:
trigger CI

The PyPI version uses the time of the last commit.
If that time was earlier than another earlier commit,
then the resulting version is lower than that from the earlier commit,
and thus the latest PyPI version might not relate
to the latest commit.
This is a quite rare situation but it can happen
when PRs are rebased and then merged.

This commit here is just to get the latest version online,
but also to raise some awareness.

commit message:
ChoiceLayer in loop without dep (#1213)

This is the case for beam search on a CTC model.
The choice of a label in one frame is independent from the earlier labels.

Determining the best sequence actually is trivial in such example,
and does not require beam search at all. Just pick the argmax in each frame.

But what about beam_size then?
We expect that we get out a beam of this size.
So we need to get the N best sequences, not just the best.

How can we efficiently do that?
I think this again needs some global search.

I was thinking more about it and I think
we really want to have the same beam search algorithm as before
to get the N best.
Also, this is not an approximation of the search
but actually the exact solution.

We also want to support conditional parameter assignments,

After quite a bit of back and forth, this is what I came up with.

This also extends the rfl.Cond logic
to support extra ops.
This is anyway nice to have.

This also extends the rfl.Cond logic
to allow None results,
which makes sense when there are potential ops
with side effects like parameter_assign.

This also extends rfl.Cond by having some callbacks,
which are used for the parameter_assign logic.
This is maybe not so nice.

This also extends the rfl.Layer by having a list of usages.
This is maybe ok.

All of this is used then by the parameter_assign logic.
The logic is not really nice and easy to understand,
but I currently don't really have an easier solution.

commit message:
Torch ONNX export, proper dynamic dims handling (#1362)

This implements proper dynamic dims handling as it was discussed #1333. It also extends some test cases and documentation.

- Test cases: Also perform ONNX inference on the exported ONNX models.
- Handle `available_for_inference` in `extern_data`: They are excluded.
- Handle duplicated dims in `extern_data`: Only the first is used. (First according to the order defined by the dict in the config.)
- Handle scalar dynamic dims in `extern_data` and `model_outputs`: They are excluded.
- It is an error if some dim `dyn_size_ext` in `model_outputs` is specified as not being a scalar (e.g. common seq lens of shape [B]) but its value is not defined.
- Demos are adapted.
- Torch-to-ONNX export documentation extended.

commit message:
RETURNN frontend native helpers (#1403)

Some of the most often called functions (`Tensor._raw_backend`, `rf.combine`, `rf.compare`, etc) are replaced by native pure C++ implementations.

For #1402.

* [x] `rf.combine` -> `tensor_combine`
* [x] `rf.compare` -> `tensor_compare`
* [x] `Tensor.__eq__`, `Tensor.__ne__`, ..., `Tensor.__add__`, ... (all in `_TensorOpOverloadsMixin`) -> `tensor_eq` etc
* [x] `rf.equal`, `rf.not_equal`, ..., `Tensor.add`, ... -> `tensor_eq` etc
* [x] `rf.logical_not` -> `tensor_invert`
* [x] `rf.abs` -> `tensor_abs`
* [x] `rf.neg` ->  `tensor_neg`
* [x] `rf.ceil` -> `tensor_ceil`
* [x] `rf.floor` -> `tensor_floor`
* [x] `Tensor._raw_backend`
* [x] `Tensor.raw_tensor` setter
* [x] `Tensor.copy`
* [x] `Tensor.copy_template`

I think this is good already for this PR, and already shows great speedup. We can do further work in other separate PRs.

* [ ] `Tensor.__init__`
* [ ] `Tensor.copy_compatible_to`, `Tensor.copy_compatible_to_raw`, `Tensor.copy_compatible_to_dims`, mostly reusing the same logic as in `combine` and `compare` if possible, but then also falling back to the generic code
* [ ] `Dim.__init__`
* [ ] `Dim.__eq__`
* [ ] `Dim.__hash__`

commit message:
Torch opt param groups configurable

Three variants how this can be configured by the user in the optimizer options dict:

- ``param_groups_custom``: callable which returns a list of param groups.
  This is the most flexible option, and could also go beyond just weight decay logic,
  or having more than two param groups (weight decay disabled/enabled).
- ``weight_decay_custom_include_check``: callable which returns True/False for each param,
  to either include it in the weight decay group or not,
  or None to use the default logic.
- ``weight_decay_modules_blacklist``: list of modules types which should not get weight decay.
  Those can be RF modules or pure PyTorch modules.
  The types can be specified as string (e.g. ``"torch.nn.LayerNorm"``) or as the type itself.

author: Nahuel Unai Roselló Beneitez <31628502+Icemole@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
HDFDataset, use bisect in _get_file_index() (#1532)

Optimize temporal complexity of `_get_file_index()`.

Helps in managing the training of big datasets (#1519).

Tests in a big dataset (1000 - 2000 HDF files, ~28 M segments) show that the time taken went from 50 minutes down to 15 minutes (approximately).

This code has been previously tested with an assertion that all file indices returned by the current implementation should be equal to those returned by the previous implementation. Either way, I think the implementation makes enough sense by itself.

As per `numpy.searchsorted` vs `bisect.bisect`, I looked into this, and it seems that `searchsorted` fails to give the best performance in single searches nested in a loop (as shown [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62753467/is-python-bisect-faster-than-numpy-searchsorted)), which is pretty much the current use case. Either way, I assume both approaches would be fine since they would yield the same temporal cost.

Note that the current temporal cost of `get_file_index` is `O(log(num_hdf_files))`. This could in theory be reduced to `O(1)` by creating a dense dictionary with all real sequence indices pointing to their corresponding file indices. However, this would imply a spatial cost of `O(num_seqs)` dumped into a single variable, which in our case would definitely be non-negligible (28+ MB for a single variable).

PS: I tried implementing the `O(1)` temporal cost approach but so far I haven't succeeded. I only invested a short amount of time on this issue so I can look into it for longer if you really want, but I find that the speedup that this implementation provides with minimal changes is really valuable.

author: Albert Zeyer <albzey@gmail.com>
commit message:
Dim math, fix potential leak (#1611)

The problem occurs when temporary other dim tags are created over and over
(in some eager-based framework like PyTorch)
and then they are combined via dim-tag math (`dim1 + dim2`),
which was cached.

* We now restrict this cache with a simple limit.
* We also use weak refs for the cache keys.
* We also reset the cache after every step.

The dim tag math changes have some not-so-obvious side effects,
which needed some minimal other extensions,
e.g. some Numpy backend implementation.

reverting the fixing behaviour.

two reasons: 1) the new behaviour is confusing for new users. Either
something is fixed, or it's not. 2) the fixing didn't work! things that
should have been fixed were passed to the optimizer for optimization.

If we really want to save keystrokes, consider this:

m.foo.fix()
m.foo.unfix()
m.foo.constrain_positive()

is the same as

m.foo.fix()
m.foo.constrain_positive()

but the latter throws a warning.

author: Moreno <morepabl@amazon.com>
commit message:
Changes in EP/EPDTC to fix numerical issues and increase the flexibility of the inference.

    Changes to avoid numerical issues and improve the performance:
    - Keep value of the EP parameters between calls
    - Enforce positivity of tau_tilde
    - Stable computation of the EP moments for the Bernoulli likelihood
    - Compute marginal in the GP model without directly inverting tau_tilde

    Changes to improve the flexibility:
    - Add parameter for maximum number of iterations
    - Distinguish between alternated/nested mode
    - Distinguish between sequential/parallel updates in EP

updated osx to macOS 10.15.7, JDK to 14.0.2, and XCode to Xcode 12.2 (#904)

The CI  was broken. This commit fixes the CI. The root cause is reported in more detail in issue #905.

In short, the default macOS version (10.13, see the TravisCI docs) used in TravisCI isn't supported by brew which caused the brew install pandoc in the download_miniconda.sh pre-install script to hang and time out the build. It failed even on inert PRs (adding a line to README, e.g.). Now, with the updated macOS version (from 10.13 to 10.15), brew is supported and the brew install pandoc command succeeds and allows the remainder of the CI build and test sequence to succeed.
